scope: All fifty Organic identities 4.1–4.50C for source-constrained interpretation of cross-topic 1.25 reaction-equation coverage. Read-only research; no curriculum completion decisions or promotion.
policy: Each source identity appears once; multiple source IDs can reuse a reaction case without creating new compulsory reactions.
Formula models here are representative proposals except where the source explicitly specifies the named reaction or repeat model. They are not copied publisher questions.
Components derive from visible C suffix/bold restriction: 4.29C–4.43C and 4.48C–4.50C are Paper 2C only; 4.44–4.47 are shared.
A standard molecular equation, structural equation, displayed diagram, practical plan, classification task and no-reaction observation prove different skills; do not collapse them.
States require actual conditions and mixtures. A deliberately state-free structural model is not automatically full state-symbol evidence under 1.25.
Do not invent compulsory mechanisms: 4.6 and 4.22 explicitly exclude mechanism knowledge; 4.26 excludes cis/trans or E/Z notation.
[O] is limited oxidation shorthand, not a chemical substance with a state; esterification has no [O] reagent.
A printed polymer repeat equation is ideal repeating-chain shorthand; finite end-group counts require separate assumptions.
